2027-04-27.title: Tuesday of the fourth week after Qyomtho · St Cletus, Pope
readings: A kingdom that cannot be shaken
The rich ruler; “we have left our homes and followed you”
2027-04-27.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. The Panchangam remembers St Cletus, Bishop of Rome.
2027-04-27.verse: Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us give thanks, by which we offer to God an acceptable worship with reverence and awe
theo: Kerala knows what it is for the ground to shake. Many of us remember the floods of 2018, when houses built over a lifetime were gone in a night and families learned how little of what they owned could really be kept. The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of a greater shaking. God's voice once “shook the earth” at Sinai, “but now he has promised, ‘Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.’” This phrase, Hebrews explains, “indicates the removal of what is shaken... so that what cannot be shaken may remain.” Everything made will one day be tested. And then comes the good news: “Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us give thanks, by which we offer to God an acceptable worship with reverence and awe; for indeed our God is a consuming fire.” The kingdom of the risen Christ is the one thing that will not be washed away. The fitting response is thanksgiving and worship, which is exactly what the Holy Qurbono is: the great thanksgiving of the Church. But Hebrews also warns: “See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking.” God still speaks, from heaven, through his Son.

The Gospel shows a man who heard that voice and could not let go of what shakes. “A certain ruler asked him, ‘Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?’” He has kept the commandments since his youth, and he is sincere. Then Jesus says: “There is still one thing lacking. Sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.” Luke records simply: “he became sad; for he was very rich.” He was holding on to the house that the flood would take. Jesus looks at him, not with anger but with sorrow, and says: “How hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!” The listeners ask, “Then who can be saved?” and he answers, “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.” Then Peter speaks for the Twelve: “Look, we have left our homes and followed you.” Jesus' reply is one of the most generous promises in the Gospel: “there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children, for the sake of the kingdom of God, who will not get back very much more in this age, and in the age to come eternal life.” What we let go of for Christ is not lost; it is placed in the one kingdom that cannot be shaken.

Today the Panchangam remembers St Cletus, one of the first Bishops of Rome after St Peter. St Irenaeus of Lyons, writing in the second century, lists the succession at Rome: after the apostles Peter and Paul came Linus, then Anencletus (Cletus), then Clement (Against Heresies III.3, in substance). Later tradition counts Cletus among the martyrs. We know very little more about him, but what we know is precious: he received what Peter had handed on and passed it on faithfully. He belongs to the unshakable kingdom because he built on the rock. Our own Church, since the reunion of 1930, lives in full communion with the Successor of Peter, and so we honour the early Bishops of Rome as fathers in the faith. Today, pray for the Pope and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our bishops. And look at your own life after the readings: what are you holding on to that could be shaken away in a night? Let go of one thing this week, give something to the poor, and offer thanks at the Qurbono for the kingdom you are already receiving.

2027-04-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you give us a kingdom that cannot be shaken. When the earth and the heavens are shaken, you remain. Deliver us from clinging to what passes, as the rich ruler clung to his wealth, and give us the courage of Peter and the apostles who left everything to follow you. By the prayers of St Cletus, who received the faith from your apostle Peter and handed it on faithfully, keep your Church firm on the rock, and bless our Holy Father the Pope and the bishops of our Church. Let us offer you, with reverence and awe, the worship of thanksgiving. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the thanksgiving of those who are receiving an unshakable kingdom: on the altar the Lord gives us his Body and Blood, the treasure in heaven already given on earth.

quick: Hebrews: God will shake earth and heaven so that what cannot be shaken may remain; we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, and we respond with thankful worship.
The rich ruler went away sad because he was very rich; Jesus promises much more to those who leave everything for the kingdom.
St Cletus, an early Bishop of Rome after St Peter, faithfully handed on what he had received.
2027-04-27.action: Give away one thing you are attached to, to someone who needs it.
2027-04-27.question: What am I holding on to that could be shaken away in a night?

family.explain: A rich man asked Jesus how to live forever with God. Jesus said: give your riches to the poor and come, follow me. But the man was sad because he loved his things too much. Peter said: we left everything to follow you! And Jesus promised that God gives back much more to people who follow him. Things can break or be lost, but God's kingdom lasts forever.
family.intention: We pray for people who lost their homes in floods, fires or wars.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing in our house we could give to someone who needs it more?”

illus: In August 2018 a family near Chengannur lost almost everything to the flood. When the water went down, the father walked through the house: the furniture was ruined, the photographs gone, the car useless. In a high cupboard he found the family Bible and the small cross his mother had kept, both dry. That evening the family, staying in a relief camp in the parish hall, prayed the evening prayer with the cross propped on a chair. The youngest daughter asked why they were thanking God when they had lost so much. Her father said: we are all alive, we are all together, and God is still God. That is what the water could not take.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you give us a kingdom that cannot be shaken. Loosen our grip on what passes. Amen.
share: See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking (Hebrews 12:25). Where is God speaking to me now, and am I listening?
There is still one thing lacking (Luke 18:22). What is the one thing still lacking in me?
Look, we have left our homes and followed you (Luke 18:28). What have I left for Christ, and what has he given back?
interc: For all who have lost homes and possessions in floods, fires and wars, that they may find help and hope.
For the rich, that they may be generous and detached in heart.
For the Pope, the successor of St Peter and St Cletus, and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and bishops.
For priests, religious and missionaries who have left home and family for the kingdom.
For our parish, that we may give thanks with reverence and awe at every Qurbono.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you give us a kingdom that cannot be shaken. Release us from all that holds us back, keep your Church firm on the faith of the apostles, and let us offer you a worship of thanks with reverence and awe. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Hebrews tells us that God will shake not only the earth but also the heaven, so that what cannot be shaken may remain (Hebrews 12:26–27). Many of us remember the floods of 2018. We learned then how quickly things can be swept away.

But there is something that will never be swept away: since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us give thanks, by which we offer to God an acceptable worship with reverence and awe (Hebrews 12:28). That thanksgiving is the Holy Qurbono.

The rich ruler asked Jesus about eternal life, but when Jesus said, sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor... then come, follow me, he became sad; for he was very rich (Luke 18:22–23). Peter said, look, we have left our homes and followed you, and Jesus promised: no one who has left house or family for the kingdom of God will fail to get back very much more in this age, and in the age to come eternal life (Luke 18:28–30).

Today we remember St Cletus, one of the first Bishops of Rome after St Peter, who handed on faithfully what he had received. He built on the rock. Let us pray for the Pope and our bishops, let go of one thing that holds us back, and give thanks at the altar for the kingdom that cannot be shaken. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever built a sandcastle, and then a wave came and washed it away? Many things in this world are like that sandcastle. But Jesus gives us something that no wave can wash away: God's kingdom and his love. A rich man was sad because he did not want to share his things. But Peter left everything to follow Jesus, and Jesus gave him much more. This week, can you share one toy or book with someone who needs it?

My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.

points.h: A kingdom that cannot be shaken
sub: St Cletus and the Church built on the rock.
q: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth should change, though the mountains shake in the heart of the sea
And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
points.apply: Pray today for the Pope and for the bishops of our Church.

sub: Much more in this age, and eternal life.
q: Now the Lord said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father’s house to the land that I will show you.”
More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.

concl: Everything that can be shaken will pass; the kingdom of the risen Christ remains.
What we leave for Christ is not lost; it is kept in his kingdom and given back many times over.
2027-04-27.resolve: Listen to the one who speaks from heaven, loosen your grip on what passes, and give thanks at the altar for the kingdom that cannot be shaken.
